annotation.title_clean: Tanggungjawab Perubatan dalam Pembedahan yang Dibantu Robot Menurut Perspektif Etika Islam dan Fiqh
annotation.title_en: Medical Responsibility in Robot-Assisted Surgery from Islamic Ethical and Fiqh Perspectives
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yunos, A.S.; Wan Saifuddin, W.M.S.; Hamdan, M.N.; Baharudin, M.H.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative fiqh study of medical responsibility in robot-assisted surgery, applying classical Islamic concepts (ḍamān, taʿzīr, qiṣāṣ, direct vs indirect causation) to surgeons, medical teams, manufacturers, hospitals and maintenance engineers. Proposes a Shariah-compliant accountability model ensuring justice, patient safety and trust.
key_provisions_or_claims: Medical responsibility in robotic surgery is defined as legal liability in qiṣāṣ, taʿzīr or ḍamān borne by the surgeon or equivalent parties.
Liability is distributed among surgeons, medical teams, manufacturers, hospitals and maintenance engineers.
Hospitals bear ḍamān for negligence in training, maintenance, supervision, and must ensure transparent marketing and data accuracy.
Surgeons must be competent; otherwise the contract is void and ḍamān with fee refund applies.
Proposes a comprehensive Shariah-compliant accountability framework for robotic surgery.
